data.cultural_impact: The name Cleve has Anglo-Saxon origins, and in Old English, clef means 'cliff' or 'Promontory'. This name might have been derived from the Anglo-Saxon name "Clefweard," which means 'ruler of the cliff.' In the context of English history, the name may have been associated with powerful and protective figures, as cliffs could symbolize strong defenses against the elements and adversaries.
